fluxsim init.description: Write a small FLUX bundle and its FLUID contract into a directory, so a first run needs nothing else checked out. With --contract and --profile, write a bundle for your own data instead: the contract, and a Simulation declared from the profile's published aggregates, with every number labelled in its parameter register (from the profile, from the contract, or assumed, with the reason). The directory must not exist yet, or must be empty: nothing is ever overwritten.

examples.note: write a project into a new directory
or into the current directory, if it is empty
write a bundle for your own data, from its contract and its profile

actions.help: show this help message and exit
where to write the project (created if missing)
a FLUID contract: the bundle generates rows for each of its exposes the profile describes; copied into the bundle unchanged (needs --profile)

a profile document of that data (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md), such as `fluid profile` writes: the Simulation pins its digest and is declared from its published aggregates; it stays outside the bundle (needs --contract)

with --contract and --profile: write nothing, and exit 1, when a statistic the profile publishes is unused or a number rests on a gap, an assumption standing in for what the profile did not publish (docs/adr/0014); each one is named
with --strict: accept the unused statistics of the profile, or the gaps of the Simulation, at or below this JSON Pointer; repeatable, and refused when it accepts nothing
emit machine-readable JSON

fluxsim plan.description: Execute the whole pipeline once, in memory, and write down what it saw: inputDigest, the seed-tree paths it materialised, the per-emit seam digests, and each declared fidelity block as it compiled, every epsilon included. Writes plan.json and seed-paths.ndjson under the run directory.

examples.note: record what a run would do
keep the run state somewhere else
plan the run under kernel 0.2.0

actions.help: show this help message and exit
path to the FLUX bundle directory
which Simulation document to resolve (default: the bundle's only one)
declared run zone, for sovereignty checks

the kernel the new plan takes, one of 0.1.0, 0.2.0 (default 0.1.0). The plan records it, and apply, replay, verify and ship run the kernel their plan names; 0.2.0's streams are counter-based and its continuous draws binary64 (docs/spec/KERNEL-SPEC-2.md), so its digests differ from 0.1.0's

the most processes that may generate the rows of an emit declared by statistics: a number (never more than one per CPU) or auto for one per CPU; the run summary says how many it used, and the rows and every digest are the same whatever the number (default: FLUX_JOBS, else 1)

refuse the run when a column falls back to a type default (an optional column nothing maps onto, a DATE or TIMESTAMP column with no declaration of its own), with a table of every such column, before any row is drawn; a Simulation can ask for the same with strictCoverage: true in its extensions; without either the plan names those columns and goes on, and with this flag the rows and every digest are the same either way
the profile document the Simulation pins under extensions['com.agentics.flux/1'].profile (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the Simulation pins none
run-state directory (default: ./.flux)
emit machine-readable JSON

which Simulation document to resolve (default: the bundle's only one)
declared run zone, for sovereignty checks

the most processes that may generate the rows of an emit declared by statistics: a number (never more than one per CPU) or auto for one per CPU; the run summary says how many it used, and the rows and every digest are the same whatever the number (default: FLUX_JOBS, else 1)

refuse the run when a column falls back to a type default (an optional column nothing maps onto, a DATE or TIMESTAMP column with no declaration of its own), with a table of every such column, before any row is drawn; a Simulation can ask for the same with strictCoverage: true in its extensions; without either the plan names those columns and goes on, and with this flag the rows and every digest are the same either way

the profile document the Simulation pins under extensions['com.agentics.flux/1'].profile (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the Simulation pins none; read only for a fresh plan, so refused with --run-id

fluxsim run.description: Plan and apply in one call, then optionally verify, write every stream to a sink, and ship. Stops at the first stage that exits non-zero; the artifacts of every stage that did run are still returned under that stage's own key.

examples.note: plan, apply, verify and ship in one command

fluxsim verify.description: Re-check an applied run on five independent legs: the run's own artifacts against its recorded digest, the golden regression, row conformance against the referenced contract, the RFC-04 enforcement vectors, and every declared fidelity check. One line per leg, with the flag that turns a `not checked` leg into a result. A run whose plan pins a profile is also scored against it, per property, table, dimension and overall, when the profile is passed with --profile.

examples.note: re-check an applied run on five independent legs

actions.help: show this help message and exit
path to the FLUX bundle directory
the run id to act on (as reported by `fluxsim plan`/`fluxsim run`)
record this run as the golden baseline (requires --reason)
why the golden baseline is being updated

the committed real-data slice one expose's fidelity check is measured against, as EXPOSE_ID=file://PATH; repeatable, once per expose; the file holds one JSON object per line, keyed by the expose's contract column names (e.g. {"subscriber_id": "s-1", "amount": "12.50"})

the profile document this run's plan pins (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md): every declared fidelity property with no --committed-slice is checked against it, and the run is scored per property, table, dimension and overall (docs/spec/SCORECARD-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the run pins none
compare each emit's means with the pinned profile on a sample: FRACTION of its blocks of records, each mean decided by its 95 per cent interval (docs/spec/SAMPLE-SPEC.md)
records in a block of the sample (default: 1000); needs --sample
seed of the choice of blocks (default: 0); needs --sample
path to an RFC-04 vectors file
exit 0 even when the bundle's declared golden.baselineDigest does not match this run's runDigest
file holding the 32-byte ed25519 seed a prior `fluxsim ship` signed with; its public half becomes the trust anchor, and the check says it is self-attested

file holding the 32-byte raw ed25519 PUBLIC key (raw or hex -- the `publicKey` a fidelity record prints) any fidelity record this run already holds is checked against; without it, and without --signing-key, the signature is reported as not checked
run-state directory (default: ./.flux)
emit machine-readable JSON

fluxsim ship.description: Run the fidelity gate over every emit that declares a fidelity block, and only if none is withheld, pack the bundle and the run into one evidence archive with its in-toto statements. A run whose plan pins a profile needs it with --profile: it is gated and scored against it, and its scorecard travels in the archive.

examples.note: pack the evidence archive
a bundle that declares a fidelity block needs the slice it is measured against

the profile document this run's plan pins (docs/spec/PROFILE-SPEC.md): every declared fidelity property with no --committed-slice is checked against it, and the run is scored per property, table, dimension and overall (docs/spec/SCORECARD-SPEC.md); refused when its digest is not the pinned one, and when the run pins none
file holding a 32-byte ed25519 seed (raw or hex) to sign fidelity records with; without it the record is signed by a per-invocation key and says so

file holding the 32-byte raw ed25519 PUBLIC key (raw or hex -- the `publicKey` a fidelity record prints) the gate checks the record's signature against; without it the record is checked against the public half of the key that signed it and says it is self-attested
